name: Lungta Drift Waxed Canvas Motorcycle Jacket
description:
A waxed canvas motorcycle jacket from Lungta, a street brand operating out of a converted rail workshop in the old Pilsen neighborhood. The silhouette is asymmetric zip closure with a wide lapel that can be worn open or snapped flat. Reinforced shoulders and elbows with sewn-in impact foam panels — not rated for high-speed crash protection, but enough to matter in a fall. Two slash pockets at the hip, a single chest pocket, and a hidden interior pocket along the right panel. Available in a deep tobacco brown or a nearly-black olive.

Lungta makes about 200 jackets a year. They don't advertise. You find out about them through someone who wears one, or you don't find out. The wax treatment is done by hand in-house and needs refreshing every season — a ritual that owners take seriously. The jacket develops a personal patina over years of wear that makes each one look different from every other one. Tier 3 riders and Tier 2 couriers both wear them; the price point is a stretch for the latter but considered worth it.
materials: impact foam shoulder and elbow inserts
what_it_says: You found something real and you take care of it. You're not the kind of person who replaces things when they can be maintained.
worn_by: anyone who knows someone who wears one
story_hooks: Lungta's head maker, a woman named Dayo Lindqvist, has been approached by two separate mid-tier fashion labels wanting to license the design. She has turned both down, and the second approach came with a threat she didn't expect.

The impact foam panels are sourced from a single supplier — a small Tier 1 materials reclaimer who pulls the foam from decommissioned transit seating. If that supply dries up, Lungta stops making the jacket as currently designed.

A Tier 4 collector has been buying Lungta jackets through intermediaries and reselling them at triple the price in Spire-adjacent markets, where scarcity and street provenance are luxury signals. Dayo doesn't know yet.
